correctness.rationale: The labelled graph formulas were validated to have 16 vertices, degree six, two common neighbors per distinct vertex pair and diameter two. Exact exhaustive enumeration of every one of 65536 detector subsets per graph gives the displayed 17 coefficients. One standalone C++17 program uses BFS-based full ordered rank partitions; a separately implemented Python program uses ternary pairwise comparisons and adjacency-derived distances. Both passed and independently recovered the maximal noncentroidal obstruction census, all optimal token-jump exchange edges, connectedness and eccentricity five from each optimum. Algebraically factoring the difference yields 12z^5(z+4)(z^2+4z+8) and the strictly positive Bernoulli reliability difference. The claim is finite; no random sample substitutes for exhaustive evidence.

originality.rationale: The foundational centroidal paper provides ranking definitions and general bounds but no Shrikhande/rook polynomial or exchange census. The closely relevant identifying-code paper studies closed-neighborhood separation rather than relative sensor ranks. The accessible published global locating-dominating record on exactly these two graphs lists minimum GLD code counts 1488 and 1872, which are not the centroidal counts 1728 and 2112; its statements do not furnish all-cardinality centroidal polynomial or sensor-basis exchange geometry. Actual literature and mathematical-record queries yielded no covering exact statement. This is a best-knowledge priority assessment, not a guarantee against unindexed historical coverage.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier centroidal sensor-placement tables or historical computer enumerations might cover these exact polynomials.
The published source on identification-code exchanges is a distinct invariant; a currently unknown general reduction might nevertheless imply part of the centroidal configuration census.
Further published theses or paywalled surveys may contain exact pair-specific counts not surfaced in inspected records; the negative search is not an exhaustive bibliographic proof.

value.rationale: Sensor placement under relative-distance-only feedback is a motivated graph identification problem. For the canonical nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs with identical (16,6,2,2) parameters, the full polynomial separates graphs despite their identical local counts, and its factorization proves a strict, all-probabilities reliability ordering. Complete minimum-basis counts, inclusion-maximal failure-spectrum, worst-case nine-detector guarantee and exact exchange geometry offer coherent combinatorial insight into sensor redundancy and relocatability. This is a natural full classification rather than a small artificial parameter slice.
